title: Tamsin and the Trail
premise: Wren Vane, a desert ranger who has spent fifteen years outrunning his family's name and a broken engagement, is sent upriver to find a lost expedition led by cartographer Tamsin Ellery, who turns out to be alive, stranded, and hunting the same thief who stole her father's survey maps—maps that prove Wren's own family fraudulently claimed the riverlands generations ago. As monsoon floods trap them together, Wren must choose between protecting the inheritance he never wanted and helping Tamsin restore hers, while the thief closes in with the only radio. In the end, Wren surrenders his name to the flood, testifies against his kin, and chooses an unmapped life beside Tamsin rather than the duty that hollowed him.
about_author: Mara Thackeray is the pen name of a former river guide who spent six seasons on the northern waterways before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who measure their lives in landscapes.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Establishes his solitary patrol life in the desert borderlands, his ritual of measuring days in distance, and the radio call that shatters it: the Ellery expedition has gone silent upriver. Command orders him to go because he knows the water. Emotional beat: reluctance—the past knocking on a door he bricked over.

chapters.title: The Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. He sets off alone in a borrowed boat with hairline cracks in the hull and storm clouds stacking on the horizon. Flashbacks reveal he once loved a woman named Tamsin Ellery—or thought he did—and fled before her father could name him heir. Emotional beat: dread layered over old grief.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Water
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Stranded at a burned campsite with two injured crew members, she signals with a signal fire as the first rain falls. She doesn't know the boat approaching belongs to the man who abandoned her fifteen years ago. Emotional beat: fierce competence masking exhaustion and fear for her missing father.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The reunion is cold; Tamsin needs his boat, not his apologies. She reveals the expedition was attacked by a thief called Corvus, who stole her father's maps—surveys proving the Vane family's land claims were forged. Wren realizes his name is the crime scene. Emotional beat: hostility sharpened by shared danger.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They run the rising rapids toward a downstream trading post where Corvus may have sold the maps. A near-capsize forces Wren and Tamsin into reluctant teamwork, and old rhythms of trust resurface despite them. Emotional beat: grudging respect kindling something neither will name.

chapters.title: The Trading Post Ledger
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the post they find Corvus passed through—but so did a Vane family agent, buying silence. Tamsin confronts Wren: was he sent to bury the truth? He admits command ordered him to confirm the expedition dead, not rescue it. Emotional beat: betrayal, then a choice—he burns his orders.

chapters.title: Monsoon
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The storm traps them in a cliff cave with the injured crew as the river swallows the lowlands. Sheltered and stripped of escape, Wren finally tells the whole truth about why he ran—his father demanded he sign the fraudulent claim as heir. Emotional beat: confession, forgiveness beginning, love rekindling against all sense.

chapters.title: Corvus
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The thief tracks them to the cave—not for money, but because Corvus is the Vane agent's hired blade, sent to erase every witness. A night fight in the flooded dark; Tamsin saves Wren's life, and they capture Corvus along with proof of the family's crimes. Emotional beat: survival fused into partnership.

chapters.title: The Name I Carried
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Floodwaters receding, they find her father alive but dying at a mission upstream; he entrusts the recovered maps to both of them. Wren resolves to testify publicly against his own blood, surrendering the Vane name forever. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into inheritance of a truer kind.

chapters.title: Unmapped
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Months later, Wren stands before the inquiry, speaks the truth, and walks out of the courthouse lighter than he's ever been. Tamsin waits with a new boat and blank charts. Together they set off upriver to survey honestly what was stolen dishonestly. Emotional beat: resolution—love chosen freely, identity rebuilt from current, not ancestry.
